## 1. The question

We are precomputing one Surface-1 "sub-universe" blob per target subawardee (the pre-call brief /
on-call console payload). Two sizing questions drove this analysis:
1. **How big is the target universe** we actually build blobs for — and how does a materiality /
   relevance filter change it?
2. **What does each blob cost** (size, build time) and what is the serve latency?

The batch input in the frozen contract is **56,672** 5y-active subawardees (`edge_count_5y > 0` in
`gtm_prime_sub_pairs`). This analysis probes trimming that set to the real GTM universe.

## 2. Source datasets (Lance, R2 `s3://data-sink/active/`) + versions

| Dataset | Grain | Version (2026-07-07) | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gtm_sub_profiles` | 1/sub_uei | **v2** | `sub_amt_60mo` (5yr sub $), `n_lanes_lifetime`, `n_distinct_primes_lifetime` |
| `gtm_prime_combo_lanes` | uei×naics×psc | **v4** | `prime_obl_60mo` (5yr prime $), summed per uei |

| `gtm_sub_combo_lanes` | sub_uei×naics×psc | (live) | sector composition (dominant NAICS by sub $) |

Lance is versioned; re-running `market_sizing.py` against these versions is bit-exact. **Definitions:**
target set = subs with `sub_amt_60mo > 0` (proxy for `edge_count_5y > 0`); **materiality** =
`GREATEST(sub 5yr $, prime 5yr $)` ("either as sub or as prime"); **compute proxy** = `n_lanes_lifetime`
(distinct demonstrated NAICS×PSC combos — correlates with universe breadth, per-target build cost, and
hot-blob size).

Target set: **56,229 subs** | total lane-work (compute proxy) = **256,948**.

## 3. Market sizing

### 3.1 Materiality thresholds — cutting the BOTTOM
Filtering out low-$ subs cuts COUNT a lot but COMPUTE much less: the trimmed tail is cheap (small
universes). Derivation: `market_sizing.py` §1.

| Threshold (sub OR prime 5yr $) | Targets | % kept | Lane-work | % compute |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $0 (all active) | 56,229 | 100% | 256,948 | 100% |
| $50K | 50,839 | 90.4% | 249,565 | 97.1% |
| $100K | 44,884 | 79.8% | 240,885 | 93.7% |
| $250K | 36,408 | 64.7% | 225,523 | 87.8% |
| $500K | 30,144 | 53.6% | 210,982 | 82.1% |
| $1M | 24,251 | 43.1% | 193,651 | 75.4% |
| $5M | 13,230 | 23.5% | 144,198 | 56.1% |
| $10M | 9,635 | 17.1% | 120,071 | 46.7% |

**Reading:** materiality filtering is a **weak compute lever** (cut 57% of targets at $1M → save only
25% of compute) but a **strong relevance lever** (near-$0 subs aren't sales prospects). Anchor the
threshold on "worth a pre-call brief," not compute.

### 3.2 Sector composition of the $5M pool (13,230 subs)
Dominant sector per sub, by their sub $ delivered. Derivation: `market_sizing.py` §2.

| NAICS | Sector | Target subs |
|---|---|---:|
| 54 | Prof/Sci/Tech services | 6,790 |
| 33 | Manufacturing | 3,554 |
| 56 | Admin/Support/Waste | 1,269 |
| 23 | Construction | 852 |
| 42 | Wholesale | 242 |
| *(11 more)* | — | ~523 |

54 + 33 = ~78% of the pool. The 11 tail sectors are ~530 subs total — trimming them is marginal.

### 3.3 Cutting the TOP — by breadth ($5M pool, lane-work = 144,198)
Compute is hyper-concentrated in the widest universes. Derivation: `market_sizing.py` §3.

| Remove top (by breadth) | Subs left | % compute left |
|---|---:|---:|
| top 100 | 13,130 | 88.7% |
| top 250 | 12,980 | 80.7% |
| top 500 | 12,730 | 71.3% |
| top 1,000 | 12,230 | 58.7% |
| top 2,000 | 11,230 | 42.8% |

Breadth distribution ($5M pool): **p50 = 5 lanes, p90 = 25, p99 = 86, max = 582**; only **102 subs
have ≥100 lanes**, 19 have ≥200. The top 500 widest (3.8% of subs) carry **29% of compute**.

### 3.4 The widest subs by name — the reseller/distributor/staffing finding
Derivation: `market_sizing.py` §5. The extreme-breadth subs are **horizontal channel players**, not
focused capability subs — their breadth comes from selling commodity product/labor across the whole
market:

| Company | Lanes | Sub $5y | Primary NAICS | Type |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| CARAHSOFT TECHNOLOGY | 582 | $1.90B | 541618 | IT reseller/aggregator |
| CDW GOVERNMENT | 447 | $410M | 423430 | IT reseller (wholesale) |
| DELL FEDERAL / MARKETING | 363 / 353 | $821M / $99M | 334111 | OEM |
| STERLING COMPUTERS | 354 | $577M | 334111 | IT reseller |
| GLENAIR | 303 | $186M | 335929 | components mfr |
| INSIGHT GLOBAL | 302 | $362M | 561320 | **staffing** |
| AVNET / TTI / ARROW | 260 / 253 / 229 | — | 423690 | electronics distributors |
| SHI / DLT | 248 / 244 | — | 541519 / 423430 | IT VAR/reseller |
| WORLD WIDE TECHNOLOGY | 221 | $1.29B | 541519 | IT VAR |
| CISCO / L3HARRIS | 220 / 210 | — | 334118 / 334220 | OEM |
| BOOZ ALLEN HAMILTON | 218 | $783M | 541512 | diversified SI |
| AEROTEK | 190 | $47M | 561320 | **staffing** |

**Implication (not a decision):** high breadth ≈ merchant-wholesale (`423xxx`) / staffing (`561320`) /
large OEM business models. If channel players aren't the ICP, the honest filter is **by NAICS/business
model**, not an arbitrary breadth cutoff — and it's the operator's call whether a $1.9B Carahsoft is a
target. **Cutting the top by $ would be wrong** (deletes whales); cutting by *breadth/segment* is the
defensible lever.

## 4. Blob size, serve latency, build time (Phase 3b, gated)

Probe UEI `YZBMKTR1HHL7` (Valley Tool, 5,000-node universe — a p90 breadth case). Derivations in
[`derivations/`](./derivations/); these read a persisted probe blob regenerated by `measure_blob.py`
(the blob is a ~130 MB artifact, not committed — rebuild ~14 min).

**v1 blob (flat, raw events/node) — 136 MB, disqualified.** Anatomy (`measure_blob.py`):
`demand_events` = **108.49 MB (80%)**; scalar rest 16.65 MB; win_portfolio 8.39 MB; without events =
27.72 MB; without events+portfolio = 19.34 MB → **single-digit MB unreachable at 5,000 full nodes.**

**Serve-path benchmark (`serve_bench.py`), measured — every query class is instant once loaded:**
deserialize 130 MB JSON = **398 ms**; scalar filter **0.4–2.3 ms**; event-grain "last-30-days" over
250,781 rows = **29.6 ms** (NOT the ~50–500 ms first estimated); monthly-bucket equivalent = **1.6 ms**.
The only serve cost is the size-driven first-load.

**v2 blob (two-tier: tiering + monthly buckets + mart drilldown), gated (`gate_v2.py`):**
hot blob = **8.80 MB**, ~27 ms parse; build **13.6 min** (hydrate 780s→177s, material-only scans);
buckets reconcile **exactly** vs a direct demand-events mart scan; bucketed serve filter = 4.75 ms.
Trim search (`trim_experiments*.py`): monthly buckets are 18× smaller than raw; the config that lands
single-digit = material=disclosed (cap `MATERIAL_CAP`), matched_via cap 5, win_portfolio → drilldown.
**`MATERIAL_CAP` lowered 1500 → 1000** (probe 933 material = 8.80 MB ⇒ ~9.4 KB/node ⇒ 1000 keeps the
widest universes single-digit).

## 6. Decisions & the OPEN decision

**Settled (engineering):** two-surface split (Surface 1 = per-target blob; Surface 2 = `phrase.v2`
market queries); two-tier blob + monthly buckets + mart drilldown (no events sidecar dataset — it would
duplicate ~106 MB/target across overlapping universes); `MATERIAL_CAP = 1000`; no scheduled/nightly
runs (operator-triggered only).

**OPEN — operator's call, NOT decided here:**
1. **Target set / ICP filter.** Candidate cuts, in order of leverage: materiality floor (e.g. $5M →
   13,230; §3.1), sector/business-model filter (drop `423xxx` wholesale / `561320` staffing if channel
   players aren't ICP; §3.4), specific 6-digit NAICS/PSC lanes. The full 56,672 is the outer bound; the
   real GTM universe is "a few thousand."
2. **First build.** Proposed (not locked): top ~2,000 by 5yr $ — highest value + hardest size test —
   in ~2K batches, hours, no Modal. `select_top_by_value(n)` in the batch runner supports this.
